extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIH K99/R00 (Pathway to Independence) career development awards and institutional grants administrators preparing PHS 398 components
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the budget, budget justification, PHS 398 Career Development Award supplemental form sections, and responses to reviewer criticisms required for a K99/R00 (Pathway to Independence) application, including mentorship, training, and research strategy documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RESEARCH & RELATED Budget sections (A–K)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cumulative budget must include itemized sections: Section A Senior/Key Person; Section B Other Personnel (total number, total salary/wages/fringe); Section C Equipment; Section D Travel (domestic and foreign); Section E Participant/Trainee Support Costs (tuition/fees/health insurance, stipends, travel, subsistence, other, number of participants/trainees); Section F Other Direct Costs (materials and supplies, publication costs, consultant services, ADP/computer services, subawards/consortium/contractual costs, equipment or facility rental/user fees, alterations and renovations, Other1/2/3); Section G Direct Costs (A thru F); Section H Indirect Costs; Section I Total Direct and Indirect Costs (G+H); Section J Fee; Section K Total Costs and Fee (I + J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section should be completed with totals ($). The cumulative budget table on the form aggregates these values (example totals shown: Direct costs, indirects, totals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a single Budget Justification file describing personnel, travel, supplies, publication costs, and indirect cost calculations for the mentored K99 phase and indicate that an independent R00 budget will be provided upon obtaining a faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example text shows: postdoctoral fellow salary requested ($75,000/year based on NIA guidelines); mentor no salary requested; travel $6,000/year with breakdown ($1500 registration, $2000 flights, $2500 hotels/meals for two conferences/year); supplies $15,000/year (lab supplies, textbooks, sequencing fees, high-processing computer); publication costs $4,000; indirect costs calculated at 8% of Modified Total Direct Cost base rate. Only one Budget Justification file may be attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Vertebrate Animals section
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are euthanized (Yes/No). If yes, indicate whether the method is consistent with American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) guidelines; if not consistent, describe method and provide scientific justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Yes' to euthanasia, answer whether method consistent with AVMA guidelines. Provide details if exceptions are claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Program Income section
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether program income is anticipated during the periods for which grant support is requested (Yes/No). If yes, provide Budget Period, Anticipated Amount ($), and Source(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'No' leave this section blank. If 'Yes' use the specified format to report amounts and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESC) section
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether the proposed project involves human embryonic stem cells (Yes/No). If yes, list registration number(s) of cell line(s) from the NIH registry or indicate that a registry line will be used if specifics are not yet known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registry identifiers (example link: http://grants.nih.gov/stem_cells/registry/current.htm) or check the box if a specific stem cell line cannot be referenced at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — Inventions and Patents (renewals)
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewal applications, indicate whether there are inventions and patents (Yes/No). If yes, indicate whether they were previously reported (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer follow-up questions accordingly to document prior invention reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Investigator / Change of Institution section
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide names and details for former Project Director/Principal Investigator and former institution when requesting a change of PD/PI or grantee institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete name fields (prefix, first/middle/last/suffix) and institution information as indicated on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Career Development Award — Required application components
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental form requires specific sections/files including: Introduction (for resubmission/revision), Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development, Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report Publication List (for renewal), Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research, Candidate's Plan to Provide Mentoring, Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s), Letters of Support from Collaborators/Contributors/Consultants, Description of Institutional Environment, Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Resource Sharing, Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, and Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the named files (examples: Introduction_Letter_R1.pdf, Candidate_Background_R1.pdf, Specific_Aims_R2.pdf, Research_Strategy_R1.pdf, D_Responsible_Conduct.pdf, F_Resource_Sharing.pdf, D_Key_Resources.pdf). Follow the ordering and labeling conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a documented plan/file for training in the Responsible Conduct of Research as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the RCR training file (example filename D_Responsible_Conduct.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate's Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the candidate will provide mentoring to others as part of career development responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics on mentoring activities and how they fit into the candidate's training and future role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed plans/statements from the mentor(s) and co-mentor(s) describing their roles in training, mentorship, and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach sponsor/mentor letters and expand on roles, time commitments, and specific training responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support from Collaborators/Contributors/Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach letters of support documenting collaborators', contributors', and consultants' commitment to the candidate and project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should specify contributions, access to resources, training commitments, and any dedicated personnel or in-kind support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Institutional Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the institutional environment that will support the candidate's research and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a file documenting institutional resources, core facilities, and how the environment is conducive to the candidate's success (example: Institutional_Environment_R1.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Commitment to Candidate's Research Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evidence of institutional commitment to the candidate's research career development (letters, resource commitments, protected time, start-up packages, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach institutional commitment documentation (example filename: F_Institutional_Commitment.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing and Authentication of Key Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide plans for resource sharing and authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources used in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach resource sharing and key resources files (examples: F_Resource_Sharing.pdf; D_Key_Resources.pdf) describing data/resource sharing and authentication procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy and Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Specific Aims and a detailed Research Strategy describing hypotheses, aims, experimental approaches, and expected outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the research strategy includes sufficient experimental detail (statistics, numbers of animals, number of trials/replicates) as reviewers highlighted the need to add these details; attach files like Specific_Aims_R2.pdf and Research_Strategy_R1.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-evaluated criterion: Formal training in the topical field (aging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate formal training in aging and incorporation of aging-focused training activities to show fit to the funding announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable strengthening include adding aging-focused workshops, meetings, faculty on advisory committee, involvement with the Glenn Foundation, and explicit sections describing relevant training and background in aging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-evaluated criterion: Strength of supervision / mentoring plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear, specific plan for supervision and mentoring with defined roles for sponsor/co-sponsors, mentors, advisors, and assigned trainers from each collaborator's lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a table specifying what areas of expertise each mentor will provide, how involved each mentor will be for each sub-aim, the amount of dedicated time each mentor will provide for training/mentorship, and named trainees who will act as day-to-day trainers. Strengthening examples: add co-sponsors, advisors, and expanded mentor role descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-evaluated criterion: Distinctiveness of career development (not redundant with past training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that planned career development activities provide new training beyond what the candidate has already received (new skills, techniques, courses, workshops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress descriptions of prior training and expand new training elements (biochemistry, mass spectrometry, bioinformatics, creating a niche in aging) with specific courses and workshops listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-evaluated criterion: Experimental detail and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adequate experimental details including statistical methods, number of animals, number of trials, and number of replicates for each aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add statistics, sample sizes, and replicates to each aim (italicize or otherwise highlight these details). Lifespan statistics need only be included at first mention if repetitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-evaluated criterion: Feasibility / scope (avoid overly ambitious proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the scope is feasible within the award period and avoid proposing aims that collectively require too much work; consider removing or narrowing aims to create a cohesive plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example change: remove an entire aim (neuronal hsf-1) to focus the proposal into two complementary aims; provide justification of feasibility via past productivity and mentor/collaborator support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-evaluated criterion: Inclusion of caveats, pitfalls, and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Include caveats, potential pitfalls, and alternative hypotheses/experiments/methods throughout the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section should contain at least one caveat (two in some cases) offering alternative hypotheses or experiments; in the example caveats were underlined and expanded for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-evaluated criterion: Clear relationship of aims to the program focus (aging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state how each aim relates to aging and the program's goals (e.g., measuring actin integrity during aging, manipulating genes' impact on lifespan, studying chromatin state during aging).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add sub-aims and text that explicitly measure aging outcomes and connect mechanistic studies to lifespan/aging phenotypes; include a sub-aim to study chromatin modifiers in aging when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from Mentor — evidence and assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the candidate's intellectual independence from the mentor: uniqueness of research focus inside the mentor's lab, assurances about open communication, availability of strains/resources, transparency to avoid overlap, and permission to take reagents/strains and ownership of discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mentor statements guaranteeing trainees' ability to take reagents/strains and that scientific discoveries made during the mentored phase will intellectually belong to the trainee; document examples of prior trainees who transitioned to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Career Development / Training Activities — content and time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe planned training activities, time allocation, and concrete training objectives (e.g., expand skills in data science, transcriptome/ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq/proteomics, biochemistry/mass spectrometry, workshops, and courses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on how training will be obtained: in-lab mentorship (months/weeks), external workshops (Cold Spring Harbor single cell analysis, NIA Summer Training Course), institutional courses (bioinformatics classes, coding bootcamps), and collaboration-based training. Specify commitment of time (e.g., majority of award period devoted to proposed research while undertaking training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee composition and involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a scientific advisory panel with experts relevant to the proposal (aging, cytoskeleton, chromatin, bioinformatics, proteomics, biochemistry, bio-engineering) and specify their roles and meeting frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a table mapping advisory members to career training/scientific guidance roles and indicating meeting frequency for each aim (example: monthly meetings, meet every 2–3 months, full month training in a collaborator's lab, 3–6 week training blocks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Named mentor-specific training activities (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document concrete training plans with named experts/labs (e.g., full month in Eisen lab for ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq, 3–6 week training in Ting lab for miniTurbo/proximity labeling, participation in Drubin lab meetings for cytoskeleton feedback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specific duration, expected outcomes, and how the training will be integrated into the candidate's skill set; include planned frequency of meetings and presentations to mentor labs.
